Sample guide: the lemonade stand ledger

Published 5 January 2026 · Sample

Why this page exists

This guide is filler. It ships with the source code so that the guide pages, the indexes and the sitemap have something to show.

Nothing here is advice. The lemonade stand, its owner Mira and every figure were made up for the sample.

A week at the stand

Mira writes three things in a notebook each evening: cups poured, coins in the jar and lemons left in the crate.

On Thursday it rains and the notebook shows four cups. She draws a small cloud beside the line so that the low day explains itself later.

What the notebook is for

  • One line for each day, in the same order every time.
  • A mark beside any day with an unusual cause.
  • A total at the end of the week, written once.

Sample guide: labelling the rows of a garden

Published 12 January 2026 · Sample

The allotment

Plot 12 is imaginary. It has four rows, and each row gets a wooden stick with a name and a sowing week written on it.

The rows

RowCropSown in week
1Radish14
2Chard15
3Peas15
4EmptyNot sown

After the first frost

The sticks stay in the ground over winter. In spring the gardener reads them before digging, and the empty row is the first to be planted.

Sample calculator: one part as a share of a whole

Published 5 January 2026 · Sample

The rule

Divide the part by the whole and multiply by one hundred. Twelve cups out of forty-eight is a quarter of the jug, which is 25 percent.

A whole of zero has no share. The calculator says so and does not print a number.

Try it

The sample script runs in the browser and sends nothing to a server.

Sample calculator: the average for one day

Published 12 January 2026 · Sample

The rule

Divide the total by the number of days. Ninety-one watering cans over seven days is thirteen cans a day.

With zero days there is nothing to divide by, and the calculator reports that.

Sample article: the rainy Thursday

Published 6 January 2026 · Sample

Four cups

The awning leaked at two in the afternoon. Mira moved the jug under the dry corner and waited for the street to fill again. It did not.

She poured four cups that day, all of them for the postman and his cousins.

The note in the margin

That evening the notebook got its small cloud. A month later the cloud was the only reason the line made sense.

Sample article: counting the seed packets

Published 13 January 2026 · Sample

The biscuit tin

The packets live in a biscuit tin on the shed shelf. Every March the gardener tips them on the bench and sorts them by the month printed on the back.

Eleven packets this year. Two are older than the shed.

What gets sown

The old packets go in row 4 as an experiment. Nobody expects much, and the stick for that row says so.
